title: i actually have not stopped thinking about the end of @Clubbed Thumb’...
transcript: I don't think this is a hot take but I love whales this is a photo from a trip I took to Antarctica just over two years ago where one of my main goals was to see orcas in the wild and we saw so many all this to say anytime I hear a show that features whales I have to go see it when I was invited to see deep blue sound I was so excited especially because it was a Clubbed Thumb show which is one of my favorite theatre companies and the cast is literally ridiculous with MaryAnn Plunkett and Miriam Silverman but let's talk about the whales about Antarctica orcas this is about Pacific Northwest orcas and deep blue sound takes place on a small island off of the coast of Seattle and in this community there are a pod of orcas that come every single year and this year they have not shown up the mystery of the disappearing orcas is really a backdrop to this story about connection and community and how people like the ocean drift apart and come back together the  playwright abe koogler has this really beautiful way of storytelling dialogue is super rapid fire because they're jumping from person to person telling all of these different stories of this town and sharing everyone's backstories and everyone's connection and I feel like it could get confusing but I was actually so incredibly captivated and the story doesn't really have like a traditional narrative it's more of like a series of snapshots and moments from this town's life and it's only 90 minutes but I felt so connected to every single person in this town just right away it’s funny and bittersweet and just really rich and has one of those moments near the end that is so beautiful that you're like this is why I love theater for this reason and I did tear up anyway this is a really beautiful piece it is one that will stick with you and it has just been extended until April 5th
